title: Essential generals
primary_topics: The six essential generals in P-Noy war on corruption: DoJ, OSG (executive-controlled), and OMB, COA, SBN, SC (constitutionally independent)
The strategic constraints P-Noy faces: he can name heads of OMB and SBN this month but cannot appoint a majority of SC justices or name a new CJ during his term
CJ assessment of Solicitor General Jose Anselmo Cadiz -- and the OSG checkered record thus far
sub_topics: Cabinet Cluster on Good Governance and Anti-Corruption insufficient alone; need six government entities

Executive-controlled: (1) DoJ -- investigation and prosecution spark plug (Leila de Lima); can investigate but cannot prosecute -- that power exclusively belongs to OMB; DoJ can recommend but OMB prosecutes; (2) OSG -- legal counsel of Republic; takes over criminal cases on appeal to SC

Constitutionally independent: (3) OMB -- more powerful than single SC justice (decides alone vs collegially; can suspend or fire officials alone vs SC only collegially); (4) COA -- examine, audit, settle all government accounts; prevent and provide evidence of misuse of funds; (5) SBN -- decides OMB-prosecuted cases; acquittals unappealable and immediately executory; state may challenge only by certiorari (grave abuse of discretion); (6) SC -- ultimate decision maker
Merceditas Gutierrez suddenly surrendered after acrimonious Congress struggle -- P-Noy opportunity to name new ombudsman
P-Noy can name new SBN presiding justice when Presiding Justice Sandoval retires June 20; presiding justice has moral ascendancy despite only one vote

SC constraints: can appoint only four new justices during his term (one done -- Justice Sereno; two more after Justices Nachura June 13 and Carpio Morales June 19 retire; fourth after Justice Abad turns 70 May 14, 2014); cannot name new SC chief because CJ Corona turns 70 only Oct. 15, 2018 -- way beyond P-Noy term ending June 30, 2016
COA: P-Noy named new chair (Ma. Gracia Pulido-Tan) and one new commissioner (Heidi L. Mendoza)

Cadiz as SolGen: rated very good; could be another Cesar Bengzon or Ambrosio Padilla or Lorenzo Tañada; CJ first met Cadiz in 2003 at IBP inaugural (psychedelic choice of heroes: Kennedy, Ho Chi Minh, Mandela, Jose Abad Santos); upon becoming CJ, passed Cadiz portrait of Ho Chi Minh given by Vietnamese CJ

Cadiz checkered record thus far: SC voided Truth Commission; SC voided clause protecting investors from regulatory risks; SBN rebuffed OSG intervention in Garcia plea bargain; OSG should be added to Anti-Corruption Cabinet Cluster for better coordination

June 2011 turning point: P-Noy can name heads of OMB and SBN in addition to DoJ, OSG and COA already chosen; but cannot appoint new SC chief or majority of SC; must adjust battle plans to this reality

stances.claim: The six essential generals of P-Noy anti-graft war are DoJ, OSG, OMB, COA, SBN, and SC -- the first two under executive control, the last four constitutionally independent; the OMB is uniquely powerful (decides alone; can suspend or fire officials alone) and is more powerful than a single SC justice.
stances.rhetorical_move: six-generals framework establishing the complete anti-graft institutional ecosystem

stances.claim: June 2011 is a turning point because P-Noy can now name the heads of OMB and SBN (in addition to DoJ, OSG, COA already chosen), but he cannot appoint a new SC chief or numerically dominate the Court -- requiring him to adjust his battle plans to this institutional constraint.

Solicitor General Cadiz is rated very good and could be a great Republic counsel -- but his record thus far is checkered by lost causes (Truth Commission voided, investor-protection clause voided, Garcia plea bargain rebuff), and the OSG should be added to the Anti-Corruption Cabinet Cluster for better coordination.

notable_anecdotes: Cadiz 2003 IBP inaugural address with a psychedelic choice of heroes -- JFK, Ho Chi Minh, Nelson Mandela, Jose Abad Santos -- prompting CJ, upon becoming chief justice, to give Cadiz the huge Ho Chi Minh portrait that was given to CJ by the Vietnamese chief justice.

The mathematical SC constraint on P-Noy: CJ Corona turns 70 only on October 15, 2018 -- two years beyond P-Noy June 30, 2016 term end -- meaning P-Noy cannot appoint a new SC chief, forcing him to work with a Court he cannot numerically dominate.

The OMB-vs-SC-justice power comparison: the ombudsman decides alone and can suspend or fire officials alone -- while the SC acts only collegially -- making the OMB appointment arguably more strategically valuable to P-Noy than a single SC appointment.

one_paragraph_summary: Panganiban maps the six 'essential generals' of P-Noy's war on corruption: the DoJ and OSG (executive-controlled) and the OMB, COA, SBN, and SC (constitutionally independent). He notes that while Justice Secretary de Lima is 'the spark plug' of the anti-graft engine, the DoJ cannot prosecute -- only the OMB can. He highlights the OMB's unique power: it decides alone (vs SC's collegial action) and can suspend or fire officials alone -- making it more powerful than a single SC justice. After Merceditas Gutierrez's sudden resignation, P-Noy has the opportunity to name a new ombudsman. He can also name a new SBN presiding justice when Justice Sandoval retires June 20. On the SC, P-Noy faces a mathematical constraint: he can appoint only four justices in the normal course (one already done -- Justice Sereno; two more as Justices Nachura and Carpio Morales retire; a fourth when Justice Abad turns 70 in May 2014). He cannot appoint a new SC chief because CJ Corona turns 70 only on October 15, 2018 -- way beyond his June 30, 2016 term end. June 2011 is thus a turning point: P-Noy can complete his generals roster with OMB and SBN heads, in addition to DoJ, OSG, and COA (newly headed by Ma. Gracia Pulido-Tan and joined by Commissioner Heidi Mendoza) -- but must 'adjust his battle plans' to the reality that he cannot dominate the SC. CJ rates Solicitor General Cadiz very good and recalls his 2003 IBP inaugural with a 'psychedelic choice of heroes' (Kennedy, Ho Chi Minh, Mandela, Jose Abad Santos), but notes a checkered record thus far -- recommending the OSG be added to the Anti-Corruption Cabinet Cluster for better coordination.
